en: One fascicle of the Dharma of the Great Sage, the Joyful Double-Body Vināyaka.
[Compiled by] Suo Guo [Yuan], Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, and Special Advancement.

The Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery—honored with a fief of three thousand households, invested with the purple robe, posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works, and awarded the honorific title of "Great Mirror" (Dajian)—reverently [composed this].

Imperial Decree for the Translation of the *Dhāraṇī-saṃgraha-sūtra*, Fascicle Eleven, Part Two: Mantra of the Body of All Devas. *Namo vinayikāśahastimukhyataye | tadyathā | oṃ vinayika vinayika vinayika vinayika traptre traptre trikā śaṅkha-hastī-śaṅkhakacitta svāhā.* Heart Mantra: *Oṃ gīrye hṛt.* Heart-of-the-Heart Mantra: *Oṃ hre hre hūṃ svāhā.* If one wishes to perform this rite of the deity:
First, one must paint an image.
One may use white tin, copper, wood, and so forth, as well as flowers and wood;
whether cast or carved, both methods are acceptable.
As for the form of the image,
it depicts a husband and wife standing in an embrace;
each is five cun tall.
Alternatively, seven inches may be used for all;
they should all be fashioned with the head of an elephant and the body of a human.
When creating these images, one must not deviate from the prescribed measurements.
Once the image has been completed,
on the first day of the bright fortnight,
one should [perform the rite] within a clean room.
Using pure cow dung, smear it to form a circular mandala of whatever size is desired.
One should then take one *śrona* (one *lì*) of clear, refined sesame oil.
Place it in a vessel of pure copper and recite the aforementioned mantra over the oil one hundred and eight times;
then warm that oil.
Thereafter, place the image in oil and install it within the mandala;
use a clean copper spoon or ladle to draw up the oil.
Perform the consecration upon the heads and bodies of the two images one hundred and eight times.
Within a single day, perform it seven times:
four times at dawn and three times at noon, totaling seven times.
Thereafter, every day he further consecrated the original oil with mantras to pour over the image.
Performing the ritual in this manner for up to seven days,
whatever his heart’s desire was, it was immediately fulfilled according to his wishes.
While performing the ritual pouring of oil, he repeatedly made vows.
Furthermore, he prepared balls of parched grain mixed with ghee and honey,
along with radish roots and a cup of wine.
As well as *modaka* sweets, seasonal flowers, fruits, and so forth—
one should offer fresh items in this manner every day.
All virtuous undertakings will be accomplished according to one's wishes.
All calamities shall be completely extinguished.
The food offered must be consumed by oneself in order to gain strength.
This is the mudrā for invitation.
Hook the two little fingers and the two ring fingers together toward the inside; then,
with the two middle fingers, hold them upright and interlace them.
Furthermore, with the two index fingers,
each held upright against the middle fingers,
and the two thumbs also held upright.
Near the side of the index finger,
move the thumb back and forth.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vāgīśvarī-vaśataya. Recite this seven times.
For the mantra of praise: Oṃ jñānaprabhātejasvati svāhā. For the concluding mantra: Oṃ vāgīśvarī-vaśataye svāhā. Recite this seven times.
The Mantra for Consecrating Water to Protect the Body: Oṃ kili kili vajra hūṃ phaṭ.
When one wishes to perform the ritual, first recite the above mantra over water seven times.
Use it to rinse the mouth.
Furthermore, take water and recite the mantra over it seven times;
sprinkle willow-branch powder upon the body, and this shall serve as protection for the person.
Thereafter, enter the recitation chamber, the place where the ritual is performed.
Bathe with the mantra: *Oṃ ana-pa-cche li pa-pa-re-na-ha*. Recite this mantra seven times over water and use it for bathing.
The Ritual for Harmonizing Vināyakas: To request all the devas to perform the Tiśula-mudrā, join the two little fingers and the two ring fingers.
Interlace the fingers within the palms;
extend the two middle fingers so that their tips touch one another;
then place each of the two index fingers upon the lower half of the first joint on the back of its respective middle finger.
Regarding the thumb:
the mantra for coming and going is:
Oṃ śodhuru paramadhanyaye svāhā. Recite this seven times.
However, if the mantra-reciter experiences terror in dreams and sees various evil visions such as those of beasts,
one should know that this is because the King Vināyaka is angry.
Upon awakening from the dream, he immediately felt shame and remorse, begging [the deity] not to be angry.
He promised that on the following day he would personally provide food and drink as an offering of thanks.
Then, using water, he rubbed the ground to create a circular altar two cubits in diameter.
As with Pāṇḍava, one may also obtain [the following]:
take five pieces of *piṣṭaka* (flour-cakes), three radish roots, and burn them until cooked over a fire.
Place flowers upon the blossoms and burn incenses such as *śrīkhaṇḍa* (white sandalwood) and *guggulu* (bdellium) within the maṇḍala.
The practitioner sits facing east on the western side of the altar.
Having recited the mantra of Maheśvara one hundred and eight times, they say aloud:
"With shame and remorse, depart well."
Having spoken thus,
the miscellaneous items from within the maṇḍala were placed upon a tray,
carried out, and discarded toward the west.
It may also be obtained from the northwest.
Recite: "Sarvayakṣarāja āveśa saṃbhajagañja.
Having spoken these words, cast it away and immediately return.
The mantra of Maheśvara is as follows:
Oṃ vītarasani parāmaridhani cchindani cchindani bhindani bhindani svāhā. Recite this mantra one hundred and eight times.
Then the mind will immediately rejoice, not merely in a dream.
However, upon awakening, if one perceives demonic activity, one should immediately perform the aforementioned rite; it is excellent.
As for the method of creating an image: the form of the image should be upright and dignified.
He has the head of an elephant and the body of a human;
his left tusk protrudes while his right tusk is broken,
and his face is slightly turned toward the left.
Its nose protrudes outward;
it has six arms,
and its upper left hand grasps a sword.
Next, the left hand holds a fruit platter;
the lower right hand holds a wheel;
and the upper right hand holds a staff.
Next, the hands grasp the cord;
the lower hands grasp the fangs.
In creating this image, one must not deviate from the prescribed proportions.
Provide the required number of copies;
whether by casting, carving, or painting, any of these methods are acceptable.
This concludes the Great Sage’s Great Secret Essential Dharma.
This is rare among humans.
Truly, do not transmit it; you should be cautious and careful.
*The Great Sage’s Joyful Heavenly Method of the Twin-Body Vināyaka*, one fascicle.
